# the contributor audit of the global unique-noncentral inverse branches

Source: `candidate f3fa42be402ec02b`,
Sections1--7. Verdict: PASS. the contributor reran the full updated exact checker:
284 checks PASS. No different-split exclusion follows automatically.

The normalized reciprocal heights x,y,z,w are positive and sum to1.
Their actual centroid formulas give the four identities(5). Because
A>0 and B<=0, K=xy-zw>0, N=zw>K^2, and A<K. The excluded equations
give K<G,D. Subtracting the two true product equations E1,E2 shows
2K cannot equal delta: that would force Q(K)=0, while Q(A)>0 and
Q'>0 for K>A. The exact expression N-K^2=KQ/(delta-2K) therefore
forces 2K<delta. No zero denominator or sign branch was discarded.

Conversely the displayed positive inverse coordinates on
I=(A,min(G,D,delta/2)), together with H=1, give E1=E2=0 by the
full quintic identities. Reversing their nonzero-denominator product
equations gives xy=N+K and zw=N. Thus they really are the unique
normalized reciprocal coordinates of an actual section with prescribed
centroid, and K is recovered from them. Roots are not merely candidates
of an elimination equation. I independently checked the formula chain;
the exact checker verifies every stated common-denominator identity.

The convexity proof retains all parameter boundaries. KQ is positive,
increasing, and strictly convex for K>A; multiplying by the positive
increasing convex reciprocal delta-2K gives the same for R. For x,
the two displayed simple-pole coefficients at A and delta/2 are
strictly positive and the remainder is affine. For y, the polynomial
division gives J''=6-2B^2(A-B)/(K-B)^3>4, J(A)=A^2, and
J'(A)=4A+AB/(A-B)>3A. This includes B=0. For z,w the product rule
and subtraction of an affine function prove strict convexity. Thus H
is strictly convex. The positive pole at the lower endpoint and the
positive numerator at every possible upper endpoint give coercivity.
The attained unique minimum implies exactly zero, one double, or two
simple roots. Coincident upper poles and unequal coordinates are covered.

The exact example's quintic factorization, rational interval signs,
upper-endpoint value, and all extraneous-root exclusions are checked.
Its two roots both yield actual sections by the proved converse.

For Section7, y,z,w increase on the full interval. For z the term
(1+R')/(G-K)>1 uses the actual 0<G-K<1; w is identical. At the two
ACTUAL sum-one roots, x must decrease. Therefore all ratios x/y,x/z,
x/w strictly decrease between those roots. The other captured raw
height exceeds the h height because Kx>N while Ky<=N. A third
different-split point on their line must lie beyond the larger-K root;
neither the segment nor the opposite ray changes the required signs.
The stated necessary crossing interval follows directly from q crossing
zero, r crossing past1, and s staying positive. No monotonicity of all
ratios away from the actual roots, no emptiness of every crossing
interval, and no global cross-split classification are asserted.

Section8 update: root also checked the exact probability formula
P=Z(K)J0(K)/Q(K)^2 at ACTUAL roots. Substituting
P=N(x+y-K)/[(x-K)(y-K)] and R=KQ/(delta-2K) gives it directly;
the accompanying density uses the same reciprocal normalization.
the contributor reran the updated verifier:286 exact checks PASS. The logarithmic
derivative of the displayed cross-pair product divided by T is exactly
3b_i in each log coordinate. Its negative log T term is essential;
convexity does not follow merely from this identity. Off-root centroid
preservation and a quantitative cap-probability gap remain unproved.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
